theme: GLA site-allocation and SHLAA source precedence
facts: GLA publishes a London-wide Site Allocations dataset.
GLA site-allocation boundaries are indicative and borough confirmation is required for authoritative local interpretation.
GLA Planning is the maintainer of the relevant London Datastore planning GIS products.
GLA GIS is the author of the Planning Local Plan Data package.
The London Datastore planning GIS uses custom polygons.
The planning GIS package is licensed under OGL v3.
SHLAA is a technical land-capacity assessment rather than a site-allocation exercise.
SHLAA evidence must not substitute for current borough-confirmed allocation membership.
Historic approvals or capacity assessments are temporally distinct from current policy designation.
Call-for-Sites evidence is candidate supply evidence, not an adopted designation.
Brownfield status is not equivalent to site-allocation status.
Opportunity-area membership is not equivalent to a site allocation.
Planning constraint negatives do not imply positive future-growth designation.
GLA context layers may support exact exclusions only when complete authoritative geometry is available.
Positive business scoring remains gated on borough-confirmed target-polygon binding.
